title: P.A.I.N Papper AI Naillionaires
author: JoseCarlosVillarreal
selftext:
Hi everyone,

After this week, it's clear what everybody, except the AI cult, thinks when even a superficial investigation into the numbers, financial needs, and realistic growth expectations takes place.

To me, one of the most fascinating stories is about the Paper Millionaires. I remember quite a few from the first dot-com bubble. Basically, people with nice incomes who work in high positions at tech startups. They get nice monthly paychecks, but also receive millions (now we're talking billions, WTF) in company stock on paper. So when the company goes public, they're going to be billionaires.

There are some really juicy documentaries about how this kind of crowd has been growing all across California.

Most of these people are smart, and they know they're playing on the edge. They take out loans, buy houses, and use the strong credit lines that their millions on paper give them. So they live in debt, debt even bigger than that of the classic triple-mortgaged stripper from good old 2008.

I assume this week has been really, really, REALLY painful for them. But the truth is, all of this affects everyone. And I mean everyone. I'm Spanish (from Spain, the real deal), and I know for a fact that this is going to affect my country's wealth.

So we need to point fingers at these people. Public sarcasm is an old-fashioned tool that we, the people, have always had.

So I came up with my own insult for these people. As always, maybe some other human being has had the same idea before me. So if this thing gets any credit, I have absolutely no problem sharing the non-existent profits.

So, here it is:

**P.A.I.N. (Paper AI Naillionaires)**

I hope you enjoy it! If not, I'm really sorry for making you waste five minutes going through this "ladrillo".
